area_description: New aircraft, engines, drones and on-board technology.

idea_types.name: Electric or hybrid-electric aircraft
idea_types.description: An aircraft that flies partly or fully on batteries or other electric power instead of jet or piston fuel.

rules.why_it_applies: Sets the airworthiness basis a new or modified aircraft must satisfy before it can fly.

rules.document: Annex 16 Volume I and II - Aircraft Noise and Engine Emissions
rules.why_it_applies: Sets the noise and engine emissions limits a new engine or aircraft design is certified against.
Sets how aircraft may be operated, which governs any change to how flights are planned or flown.

rules.document: Environmental protection: aviation and the environment overview
rules.why_it_applies: Explains ICAO's environmental work and how its measures fit together.

readiness_checklist: A written description of the aircraft, its mission and its range
Battery or power system data, including safety and fire protection
A plan for how airworthiness will be shown
Noise estimate for take-off and landing
Charging or energy supply plan at the airfield
Flight test plan with safety limits
Pilot training and operating limits
reviewer_questions: What range and payload do you honestly expect, and how was it measured?
How will you show the battery system is safe in a failure?
How does the design meet airworthiness requirements?
What happens to the aircraft if power is lost?
Who will operate it and how will they be trained?
idea_types.national_requirements: Check with your civil aviation authority for the national requirements that also apply.

idea_types.name: Drones and unmanned aircraft
idea_types.description: An aircraft flown without a pilot on board, remotely or autonomously, for example for delivery, survey or inspection.

rules.document: Unmanned aircraft systems guidance, including Doc 10019 Manual on Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems
rules.why_it_applies: Collects ICAO's international guidance for unmanned aircraft and remotely piloted aircraft.
Sets the common rules every aircraft must follow in the air.
Sets the airworthiness basis a new or modified aircraft must satisfy before it can fly.
Sets security standards that apply to airports, aircraft and anything used on them.

readiness_checklist: Description of the drone, its weight and what it carries
Intended use and where it will fly
How the remote pilot controls it and what happens if the link is lost
Plan to avoid people, buildings and other aircraft
Security plan for data and control link
Pilot training plan
Test flight record
reviewer_questions: Where and at what height will it fly?
What happens if the control link or battery fails?
How do you keep it away from crewed aircraft and people?
Who is responsible when it is flying?
How is the data it collects protected?
idea_types.national_requirements: Check with your civil aviation authority for the national requirements that also apply.

idea_types.name: Aircraft efficiency technology
idea_types.description: A device, material or design change that lets an aircraft burn less fuel, such as lighter parts, better wings or engine upgrades.

rules.document: Annex 16 Volume III - Aeroplane CO2 Emissions Standard
rules.why_it_applies: Sets the CO2 efficiency standard that new aeroplane types must meet.

rules.document: Annex 16 Volume I and II - Aircraft Noise and Engine Emissions
rules.why_it_applies: Sets the noise and engine emissions limits a new engine or aircraft design is certified against.
Sets the airworthiness basis a new or modified aircraft must satisfy before it can fly.

rules.document: Environmental protection: aviation and the environment overview
rules.why_it_applies: Explains ICAO's environmental work and how its measures fit together.

readiness_checklist: Description of the change and the aircraft it fits
Measured or modelled fuel saving, with method
Effect on noise and engine emissions
Weight and balance impact
Plan to show the change is airworthy
Cost and installation time per aircraft
reviewer_questions: How much fuel does it really save, and how do you know?
Does it change noise or engine emissions?
How will the change be certified as safe?
What does it cost to fit and maintain?
Which aircraft types can use it?
idea_types.national_requirements: Check with your civil aviation authority for the national requirements that also apply.
